headline: Agroparc Penedès, Gelida: large earthworks on a contested site
story: Ametller Origen is building the Agroparc, an agri-food park at Gelida, near Barcelona. According to ARA, it is planned for an area of 258 hectares and involves moving 724,482 cubic metres of earth. Neighbours organised as StopAgroparc, and environmental groups, have opposed the project.

In July 2025 the Barcelona administrative court No. 3 provisionally suspended the urban planning agreement between the company and the Gelida council in the most sensitive areas; ARA reported that the bulk of the work could not begin until it was confirmed that two eagles living in the area can be relocated. In August 2025 the Mossos d'Esquadra and the Agents Rurals found machinery working inside the area covered by the ruling, and the works were stopped; the company said it had paused them temporarily and denied breaching the ruling. In September 2025 the company said it would resume work after the court confirmed it could. On 3 August 2026 the Environmental Prosecutor's Office dismissed a complaint against the works filed by StopAgroparc and the Bosc Verd collective.

What the radar adds: earthworks change the ground surface, so repeated radar images of the site stop matching each other, and new structures reflect radar differently. The map marks where this happened and when it first appeared, so you can compare it with the dates on the timeline. Our sources do not say whether the works continue after August 2026; the most recent radar passes can show it.
